title: Is this node working, app by app?
description: One machine: is Holochain running, is each app part connected, does it hold what its peers hold, when did it last hear from them, and is the machine healthy.

panels.title: Conductors
panels.description: Whether each Holochain conductor on this machine answers, with fresh readings. A machine can run more than one; the homelab runs two, Workshop and Moss.

panels.title: Readings
panels.description: How old the oldest Holochain reading on this page is. Each conductor's exporter writes every 30 s and Prometheus collects every 15 s, so up to about 45 s is normal. If this is not green, nothing below is current.

panels.title: Apps
panels.description: How many installed apps are running, and how many are stopped or missing. Missing means Nix manages the app and Holochain did not list it.

panels.title: Connected to computers
panels.description: How many network connections this machine's conductors hold to other computers, all apps together. For the whole conductor, not per app; the table below is per app.

panels.title: Parts with nobody else
panels.description: How many of this machine's app parts have no one to talk to: lost contact, or no one else yet.

targets.expr: count(holochain:dht_state{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"} == 2 or holochain:dht_state{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"} == 3) or vector(0)

panels.title: Is each app part connected, complete and recent?
panels.description: One row per part of each app on this machine: its state, how many other computers it sees, what share of its best peer's data it holds, when it last heard from anyone, how many items it is still fetching, and how many exchanges timed out in the last 15 minutes. Click an app to see its network across every machine.

targets.expr: holochain_dht_pending_fetches{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"} * on (instance, conductor, app_id, role, dna) group_left (app_name, app_kind, part_name, network_label) holochain:dht_names

clamp_min(holochain_dht_peer_timeouts_total{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"} - (holochain_dht_peer_timeouts_total{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"} offset 15m or holochain_dht_peer_timeouts_total{node="$node", conductor=~"$conductor"}), 0) * on (instance, conductor, app_id, role, dna) group_left (app_name, app_kind, part_name, network_label) holochain:dht_names

properties.value: A clamped difference over 15 minutes rather than increase(): the counter drops when a peer is forgotten.

panels.title: Connected to others, per part
panels.description: When each app part gained or lost other computers. Below the dashed line at 1 it has nobody.

panels.title: Share held, per part
panels.description: What share of its best peer's data each connected part holds, averaged over 10 minutes. Parts with nobody to compare with have no line.

panels.title: Items still on their way
panels.description: How many items the best peer has that this machine does not have yet. A write elsewhere shows as a rise that falls back.

panels.title: Last heard from others, per part
panels.description: Seconds since each part last exchanged data with anyone. A part that never has is a gap, not a line. The dashed line is at 600 s, after which a part that knows others reads Lost contact.

panels.title: What needs a human on this machine?
panels.description: What is wrong on this machine, in words.

panels.title: Bytes in and out
panels.description: Bytes per second each conductor on this machine receives and sends, all apps together.

panels.title: Refused messages
panels.description: Messages each conductor would not accept in the last hour, usually from a peer on another version or network; the conductor log says which. Not an attack by itself.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of processor time not spent idle, over 2 minutes.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Share of memory that is not available.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: Five-minute load average divided by the number of processors. Above the dashed line at 1, work is queueing for the processor.

panels.title: Disk space
panels.description: Share of each disk that is used. Memory-backed and image filesystems are left out, and so is /nix/store, which NixOS bind-mounts from the filesystem that holds /nix.

targets.expr: max by (mountpoint) (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{node="$node", fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|overlay|squashfs|nsfs", mountpoint!="/nix/store"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{node="$node", fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|overlay|squashfs|nsfs", mountpoint!="/nix/store"})

panels.title: Disk activity
panels.description: Bytes per second read from and written to this machine's disks, optical drives left out.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Every temperature sensor node_exporter finds. A virtual machine usually has none, and this panel then says No data. The dashed line is at 85 °C.

panels.title: Host network
panels.description: Bytes per second in and out of every interface except loopback, for the whole machine.

panels.title: Time spent waiting
panels.description: Share of time some task was stalled waiting for the processor, memory or disk (the kernel's pressure stall information). Sustained waiting on memory or disk is the early sign of a machine too small for what it runs.

panels.title: Background jobs
panels.description: Watched services (services.holochain-grafana.overviewUnits) on this machine that are not running, by the name the fleet gives them.
